solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pub's been given old American coin — not guilty!

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a cent is a US coin worth one hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: A pub owner proudly displays an antique American coin and is cleared of some charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Pub and 'been given' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone found innocent in court has been declared free of blame, the plain synonym of not guilty.

clue.text: Screen gondolier perhaps unable to see

parts.note: a gondolier is an example of someone from Venice, signalled by 'perhaps'
blind means unable to see

explanation.surface: A gondolier with poor eyesight is shielded from something.
explanation.definitionFit: A slatted window shade with horizontal strips is a kind of screen against light.

clue.text: Show regret about escape and liberation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the regret word goes around the escape abbreviation

parts.note: to rue is to show regret
ESC is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone feels sorry about breaking out and being freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the regret word around the keyboard's escape key abbreviation; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue frees someone from danger or captivity, which is a liberation.

clue.text: Revealing where the pigs are eating food tin

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the pig home swallows the tin

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen
a can is a food tin

explanation.surface: Pigs in their pen are uncovered chewing through a tin of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' has the pigs' home swallow the tin; 'Revealing' looks like a verb but is the adjective, as of skimpy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty clothing is skimpy and so shows a lot of the body, which is to say revealing.

clue.text: Showing relations exchanging letters

definitions.meaning: matching or analogous, as in things related to each other
writing back and forth to each other by post

explanation.surface: Family members show they are keeping in touch by writing to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both analogous to something else and keeping up a letter-writing exchange with someone.

clue.text: Temporary address regularly used in Ethernet

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the network word, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A temporary network address is assigned on an Ethernet connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' just links the pieces; the even letters of Ethernet give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas shelter is somewhere you live for a short while, a playful home address that is only temporary.

clue.text: Former partner taken back by woman in part of house

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

indicators.note: taken back means the two letters for a former spouse are written backwards

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A woman lets her ex move back into one room of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension built onto a building is one part of the house, a room added on.

clue.text: Plant clubs joined by admirer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a lover is an admirer

explanation.surface: A sportsman's club sets up a plant, and an admirer comes along.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-growing trefoil-leaved herb grown for fodder is an example of a plant.

clue.text: An unspecified amount of notes

parts.note: so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale, a second note supplied by the same plural word

explanation.surface: A musician talks of an unknown quantity of banknotes or musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The single plural word 'notes' supplies two sol-fa notes in a row, so and me.
explanation.definitionFit: The determiner means an indefinite quantity, as in 'have a bit of cake'.

clue.text: Penitent half continued with ceremony

indicators.note: half means taking the first four letters of the word continued, also its usual abbreviation

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A sorry soul went through half a ritual and then carried on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone sorry for wrongdoing and wishing to make amends; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Specialist food shop needs extra shipment

parts.note: a deli (delicatessen) sells specialist foods
extra as an intensifier means very, as in 'extra careful'

explanation.surface: A delicatessen is waiting on an additional consignment of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignment of goods brought to a customer is a delivery, the same as a shipment.

clue.text: Drink in East Sussex town

definitions.meaning: a whiskey distilled from the grain of that name
a historic Cinque Port town on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink in a seaside town in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a whiskey made from that cereal grain and a small town in East Sussex, England.

clue.text: Average emergency call needs oxygen

parts.note: SOS is the international distress call
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A routine emergency call asks for oxygen to be sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something middling, neither good nor bad, is just mediocre or average.

clue.text: Unfamiliar visitor starts to suspect the park keeper

indicators.note: starts to means taking the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: a ranger looks after a park or forest

explanation.surface: A warden begins to suspect an odd visitor in the park.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer nobody knows is someone unfamiliar, an outsider visiting.

clue.text: Public school to see going west

indicators.note: going west in an across clue means read from right to left, backwards

parts.note: to note something is to see or notice it

explanation.surface: Someone heads west to visit a public school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is a fee-paying private school; Eton is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Berkshire college is the archetypal British fee-paying public school.

clue.text: Ordinary dormice mistreated by English

indicators.note: mistreated suggests the small rodents are knocked about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some unremarkable small rodents are badly treated by an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' scrambles DORMICE into MEDIOCR, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Of only middling quality, nothing special: ordinary is a straight synonym.

clue.text: My unit is involved in open uprising

indicators.note: involved suggests the words are tangled up, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A soldier admits his company is part of an open revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles MY UNIT; 'is' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion against those in authority, especially by sailors or soldiers, is an open revolt.

clue.text: Stand-in sets record in responsibility

indicators.note: in tells us the record goes inside the word for responsibility

parts.note: a duty is a responsibility
an EP (extended play) is a type of record

explanation.surface: A substitute is placed in charge of keeping the records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets' is only a link word; 'in' places the extended-play record within the word for responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute who acts on someone else's behalf is a deputy, a stand-in.

clue.text: Where food is served with pill before surgery?

parts.note: a tablet is a pill
an op (operation) is surgery

explanation.surface: A hospital patient is given a pill before surgery and asks where meals are served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' orders the pill ahead of the operation; the question mark flags the jokey definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper surface of a table is literally where dishes are set down at a meal.

clue.text: A route from here

parts.note: a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone describes a path leading out of this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent, at a distance from this spot: the adverb means elsewhere, gone from here.

clue.text: Agreed to put on Shakespeare finally

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

indicators.note: finally means taking the final letter of the playwright's name

explanation.surface: An acting company agrees to stage some Shakespeare at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put on' looks like staging a play, but it means wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of a deal, 'it's a deal' or 'settled' — an exclamation of assent, so agreed.

clue.text: Nearly is unable to name piece of artillery

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the last letter of the word for unable is dropped

parts.note: cannot means is unable to

explanation.surface: Someone almost fails to identify an artillery piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the final T of CANNOT, leaving CANNO.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heavy gun on wheels, of the old kind fired in battles, is a classic artillery piece.

clue.text: Gentle proposal

definitions.meaning: kind, soft or careful in manner
a formal offer, such as a bid for a contract

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken offer of marriage or business.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both soft and kind in manner and a formal offer or bid to do work.
